strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Data Encoding in C2 Channels

analytics.name: Analytic 0302
analytics.guidance: Atypical processes (e.g., powershell.exe, regsvr32.exe) encode large outbound traffic using Base64 or other character encodings; this traffic is sent over uncommon ports or embedded in protocol fields (e.g., HTTP cookies or headers).

tuning.description: Adjust to accommodate legitimate compression or encryption patterns in normal web traffic
Define expected processes initiating outbound traffic to reduce false positives
Set threshold for how far traffic deviates from baseline protocol structure or size

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: Unusual Base64-encoded content in URI, headers, or POST body

analytics.name: Analytic 0303
analytics.guidance: Custom scripts or processes encode outbound traffic using gzip, Base64, or hex prior to exfiltration via curl, wget, or custom sockets. Encoding typically occurs before or during outbound connections from non-network daemons.

tuning.description: Tune duration of multi-stage encoding + transfer operations to account for script variability
Apply user allow/block list depending on which users normally perform CLI encoding

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: Base64 strings or gzip in URI, headers, or POST body

log_sources.name: linux:syslog
log_sources.channel: Unusual outbound transfers from CLI tools like base64, gzip, or netcat

analytics.name: Analytic 0304
analytics.guidance: Processes use built-in encoding utilities (e.g., `base64`, `xxd`, or `plutil`) to encode file contents followed by HTTP/HTTPS transfer via curl or custom applications.

tuning.description: Minimum byte size of encoded strings to treat as suspicious
Number of chained processes within a short window to treat as a correlated behavior

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: base64 or curl processes chained within short execution window

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: HTTP POST with encoded content in user-agent or cookie field

analytics.name: Analytic 0305
analytics.guidance: ESXi daemons (e.g., hostd, vpxa) are wrapped or impersonated to send large outbound traffic using gzip/Base64 encoding over SSH or HTTP. These actions follow suspicious logins or shell access.

tuning.description: Use to scope encoded traffic suspicion to accounts that should not initiate transfers
Threshold for bursty outbound traffic size deviation from baseline

log_sources.name: esxi:shell
log_sources.channel: base64 or gzip use within shell session

log_sources.name: esxi:vmkernel
log_sources.channel: Outbound traffic using encoded payloads post-login

log_sources.name: ESXiLogs:authlog
log_sources.channel: Unexpected login followed by encoding commands
